subject: DPA redlines & audit evidence - CardioCloud (data transfers, subprocessors)
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cardiocloud.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@cardiocloud.com; Tom Harris <tharris@cardiocloud.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CardioCloud DPA - initial redlines and evidence request

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our legal team has reviewed Redwood's DPA and attached a first-pass redline (CardioCloud_DPA_redlines_v1.docx). A few items we'd like to confirm before we can sign:

- Audit rights: CardioCloud requires the ability to request evidence of controls (SOC 2 Type II) and the option for an annual onsite audit, or a third-party assessor review if an onsite is not feasible.
- Subprocessors: we need a current register with location (country) and purpose of processing for each subprocessor that may handle CardioCloud customer data.
- Cross-border transfers: confirm whether data originating in the EU may be processed or transferred to the US and what transfer mechanisms you rely on (SCCs, adequacy, etc.).
- Pen test evidence: a high-level summary of recent penetration testing and a redacted report or executive summary would help our security team evaluate risk.

We can share our standard DPA clauses if helpful; attached redlines are in-track with our procurement expectations. Please let us know turnaround on providing SOC 2 and a subprocessor register — we aim to finalize by mid-December.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Legal Operations
CardioCloud Inc.

Attachments: CardioCloud_DPA_redlines_v1.docx
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cardiocloud.com>
Cc: Kim Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Tom Harris <tharris@cardiocloud.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CardioCloud DPA - initial redlines and evidence request

Hi Elena — thanks for sending over the redlines and for the clear list of asks. I’ve looped in Kim (Legal) and Soojin (Security) to help narrow the items and provide the requested artifacts. Quick summary / proposed next steps: 

1) SOC 2: We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. We commonly provide a redacted PDF (PII removed) and a secure link for on-demand review. Attached is a redacted SOC2 reference (redacted_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf) — please confirm if this suffices or if you need a tighter NDA.

2) Pen test: We attach a one-page high-level executive summary of our most recent third-party penetration test (pen_test_summary_Q3_2026.pdf). For full details we typically share a redacted report under an evidence exchange NDA — happy to initiate that.

3) Subprocessor register: Attached as a CSV with current entries and processing purposes (subprocessor_register_2026.csv). High level: primary compute/serving, observability, and backups — no ad networks or analytics vendors that ingest customer content. I’ll have Soojin confirm geo locations and whether any subprocessors hold EU-resident data.

4) Cross-border transfers / transfer mechanism: Redwood relies on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) where applicable and has data flow commitments in the DPA. We can add language to explicitly call out SCCs and our optional VPC/on-prem options if CardioCloud requires data to remain in the EU.

5) Audit / onsite: We’re happy to accommodate third-party assessments and periodic audits. For onsite audits we ask that they be scoped and scheduled in advance; alternatively, we can provide a dedicated security access package and a live review with our security team. We cannot typically allow unmanaged production access, but we will support a scoped auditor engagement.

6) Execution: I’ve started a DocuSign envelope with our updated DPA that incorporates your redlines where feasible and flags items for further negotiation (link below). If you prefer AdobeSign, we can do that as well.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/1234-CardioCloud-DPA
Shared evidence folder (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example_redwood_cardio_evidence

Action items: 
- Soojin to confirm subprocessor countries and whether any subprocessors process EU-resident data.
- Kim to review the specific onsite-audit clause proposed and propose alternative language that balances CardioCloud needs and Redwood operational constraints.
- CardioCloud to confirm whether the redacted SOC 2 + pen test summary are sufficient to proceed to signature.

Happy to set a 30-min sync tomorrow if that helps move this quickly.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Revenue, EMEA & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redacted_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf; pen_test_summary_Q3_2026.pdf; subprocessor_register_2026.csv
From: Tom Harris <tharris@cardiocloud.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cardiocloud.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CardioCloud DPA - initial redlines and evidence request

Rafael, thanks for the quick turnaround — helpful. A couple follow-ups from our security team after reviewing the materials: 

- Subprocessor specifics: the CSV is useful but we need country of processing for each subprocessor and confirmation of any subprocessors that may cache or persist customer content outside the EU. Please indicate which subprocessors (if any) may store encrypted backups or logs containing customer content.
- Onsite audit clause: CardioCloud prefers an explicit right to request an annual onsite or a third-party assessment with 30 days' notice. If Redwood cannot allow onsite access, then CardioCloud will require an expanded rights-to-evidence clause (e.g., live remote sessions + evidence package). We can accept a mutually agreed scope to avoid full production access.
- SCCs: please provide the exact SCCs text you intend to rely on or point to the clause in your updated DPA.

If you can get Soojin and Kim to confirm the subprocessor locations and proposed audit language today, that would let us get legal signoff early next week.

Also — can you confirm whether Redwood stores any EU-originated customer content in object storage buckets located in the US by default? If yes, is there a way to pin CardioCloud to EU-only storage?

Thanks,
Tom Harris
Lead Security Engineer
CardioCloud Inc.
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harris <tharris@cardiocloud.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cardiocloud.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Kim Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CardioCloud DPA - initial redlines and evidence request

Tom / Elena — looping in Soojin and Kim for final confirmations; see answers below and next steps. 

- Subprocessors & locations: Soojin confirms the current register shows subprocessors in US, Ireland, and Singapore. Only our backup and observability vendor (listed in the CSV) may store encrypted backups. Those backups are encrypted at rest with customer-specific keys and logs are redacted; we do not write raw customer prompts to analytics vendors. (See subprocessor_register_2026.csv for column 'geo_processing' and 'data_persistence'.)

- EU-only storage / pinning: Redwood can offer EU-only data residency for CardioCloud via our Dedicated and Private deployment options. For the hosted plan, certain operational backups may transit US regions; we can add explicit contract language and a roadmap timeline if you require EU-only at contract signature.

- SCCs / transfer mechanism: We include the EU Commission SCCs (controller-processor module) by reference in Section 9 of the updated DPA. Kim has proposed a clause that lists SCCs and confirms Redwood as the data importer that will follow the SCC obligations. If you prefer, we can paste the exact SCC template wording into the DPA.

- Onsite audit / third-party: Kim suggests the following compromise language: CardioCloud may request a third-party assessment annually; onsite audits must be scoped and scheduled 60 days in advance, limited to non-production data access where feasible; Redwood will provide a remote evidence package and a live review session within 30 days. If CardioCloud requires physical access to Redwood-controlled datacenters, we will coordinate with our hosting partners under a separate MSA.

DocuSign status: I have updated the envelope to reflect our negotiated language and requested signatures for the DPA and supporting SOW addendum. I’ll confirm when DocuSign completes.

Next steps (owners):
- Soojin (Security): provide final annotated subprocessor register and confirm what is encrypted vs. persisted (action: Today).
- Kim (Legal): finalize the audit clause and SCC insertion text (action: Today).
- CardioCloud legal: review updated DPA and confirm whether redacted SOC2 + pen test summary are sufficient or if you want a narrower NDA exchange for full reports (action: CardioCloud).

I’ll return once the DocuSign envelope is fully executed and will upload final artifacts to the shared folder. Thanks for the collaborative review — we want to make this as smooth as possible.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Revenue, EMEA & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: updated DPA envelope (DocuSign link), subprocessor_register_2026.csv, redacted_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf, pen_test_summary_Q3_2026.pdf
